sections.h2: Where is Evansville, Indiana, and how big is it?
sections.html:
Evansville is the seat of Vanderburgh County in southwestern Indiana, on a bend of the Ohio River. It is the third-largest city in the state after Indianapolis and Fort Wayne, and it covers about 47.9 square miles.

Most of the city sits in a shallow valley ringed by low hills, with the west side on higher ground. The 38th parallel crosses the north side of town. Downtown grew from an original plat of about 200 acres and still holds early twentieth-century buildings.

The county, formed in 1818, is the smallest in southwestern Indiana and forms the core of the Evansville metropolitan area.

sections.h2: What is the history of Evansville?
sections.html:
Hugh McGary Jr. bought about 441 acres in 1812 and called the site McGary's Landing. It was renamed Evansville in 1814 for Colonel Robert Morgan Evans, incorporated in 1817 and chartered as a city in 1847.

The Wabash and Erie Canal and early railroads boosted trade, and hardwood furniture made Evansville a manufacturing center, with 41 factories by 1900. The Graham Brothers built trucks here from 1916 to 1929. In World War II the city produced 167 LSTs, the nation's largest inland output, and 6,242 P-47 fighters. The National Park Service designated Evansville Indiana's American World War II Heritage City on December 6, 2022.

Thirteen neighborhoods are listed as National Register historic districts, and the Riverside district is known for tree-lined brick streets and turn-of-the-century homes. Indiana's seller disclosure form asks whether a property sits in a locally designated historic district, so owners in these areas should be ready to answer.

sections.h2: What do census numbers say about Evansville housing?
sections.html:
Evansville is split nearly evenly between owners and renters. The Census Bureau reports 54.6% owner-occupied housing for 2020 to 2024, a median owner-occupied value of $143,100 and median gross rent of $975.

The city's population is 17.6% age 65 or older, and households average 2.12 people. Many Evansville owners are in houses that were built for larger families, so downsizing is a frequent reason to sell.

sections.h2: Who are the major employers around Evansville?
sections.html:
Health care, manufacturing and finance anchor the Evansville economy. Berry Global and OneMain Financial are headquartered here, and Escalade, Old National Bank and Shoe Carnival are NASDAQ-listed companies based in the city.

  • Health care: Deaconess Health System and Ascension St. Vincent.
  • Manufacturing and pharma: Mead Johnson and Bristol-Myers Squibb.
  • Nearby plants: Alcoa in Newburgh, SABIC in Mount Vernon and Toyota in Princeton.
  • Education: the University of Evansville, a private school founded in 1854 with about 3,050 students, and the University of Southern Indiana, a public school founded in 1965 just outside the city limits.

Chemicals make up 64% of the metro area's international exports. The Census Bureau counted about $2.85 billion in health care and social assistance receipts in the city for 2022.

With two universities, student rentals and investor-owned houses are a visible part of some neighborhoods.

sections.h2: What is the flood risk in Evansville?
sections.html:
Evansville sits behind a levee system built after the 1937 Ohio River flood. The river crested at 53.7 feet on January 31, 1937, the flood covered about 500 city blocks, and the city was placed under martial law.

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers began construction in 1939 and work was completed in 1994. According to the state historical marker, the project includes 17 miles of earth levees and concrete floodwalls and 19 pumping stations, and it protects against flood water up to 57 feet. The Evansville-Vanderburgh Levee Authority District maintains it.

  • The eastern levees closely follow I-69.
  • Pigeon Creek has been widened and leveed, and Ohio River backwater affects the whole county, according to a 2023 presentation to county commissioners.
  • That presentation notes the creek's average annual peak flow at the Fort Branch gauge rose from about 2,350 to 2,820 cubic feet per second over 35 years.

Indiana's seller disclosure asks the owner to say whether they know the property is in a FEMA flood plain. A buyer or lender may ask for flood zone and insurance details, so find out your parcel's status before you sell.

sections.h2: How hot, wet and snowy is Evansville?
sections.html:
Evansville has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and cool winters. Average temperatures run from about 32.5 degrees Fahrenheit in January to 78 in July.

Annual precipitation is about 45.3 inches, with 11.8 inches of snow. The record high is 111 degrees on July 28, 1930, and the record low is minus 23 on February 2, 1951. Cooling equipment gets more use here than it does in northern Indiana, and heavy rain is a bigger concern than snow loads on roofs and in basements.

sections.h2: What are the Evansville rental registration rules?
sections.html:
Evansville regulates rental dwellings under Chapter 15.16 of its municipal code, and the Building Commission runs a rental registry. Registration is required for substandard rental buildings and voluntary for well-kept ones.

  • Required registration fee: $100.00 per dwelling unit.
  • Voluntary registration fee: $10.00 per dwelling unit, with a signed affidavit that the building meets the property maintenance code.
  • A voluntary permit lasts one year or until title transfers, and covers up to $3,000 of maintenance work per unit.

Owners must report an ownership change within 30 days, and a prior registration expires 30 days after title transfers. Code officials may give an owner at least 10 calendar days to fix a violation, and an owner ordered to register may appeal in writing within 10 calendar days of service.

The city has moved rental registrations to an online platform. Call the Rental Registry at the Building Commission, 812-436-7887, with questions.

sections.h2: Which offices handle permits, property tax and code enforcement in Evansville?
sections.html:
City and county offices share the Civic Center Complex at 1 NW Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd., Evansville, IN 47708. The Building Commission is in Room 310, the Department of Metropolitan Development in Room 306 and the Area Plan Commission, which handles zoning and improvement location permits, in Room 312.

  • Building Commission, permits and inspections: (812) 436-7885.
  • Vanderburgh County Auditor: Room 208, (812) 435-5369.
  • Vanderburgh County Treasurer: Room 210, (812) 435-5248.

Property maintenance enforcement, including weeds, trash and existing structures, falls under the Building Commission. Indiana taxes are due in two installments, listed by the state as May 11 and November 10 for 2026, with a 5% penalty up to 30 days late and 10% after that.

faqs.q: Is Evansville in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of the city are protected by a levee system of 17 miles of levees and floodwalls and 19 pumping stations. Your own parcel's FEMA status depends on its location, so check before listing, because Indiana's disclosure form asks about it.

faqs.q: Do Evansville landlords have to register their rental properties?
faqs.a: Substandard rentals must register at $100.00 per unit, while well-maintained rentals may register voluntarily at $10.00 per unit. Call the Rental Registry at 812-436-7887 to confirm which applies.

faqs.q: When are Evansville property taxes due?
faqs.a: In May and November. The state lists May 11 and November 10 for 2026. Late payments carry a 5% penalty up to 30 days and 10% beyond that.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Evansville?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $143,100 for owner-occupied units in 2020 to 2024. Your own house may differ based on condition and neighborhood.

faqs.q: Where is the Evansville Building Commission?
faqs.a: In Room 310 of the Civic Center Complex, 1 NW Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd. The main number is (812) 436-7885.

faqs.q: What happens to a rental registration when I sell in Evansville?
faqs.a: Ownership changes must be reported within 30 days, and a prior registration expires 30 days after title transfers. The new owner registers again.
